items.observation: `stats()` and `_discoverQueues()` rebuild the key scheme by hand (`${prefix}:inflight:*`, `:queue:`, `:delayed`). If the keys.dart scheme changes, statistics silently count wrong.
items.proposed_fix: Add `inFlightPattern()`, `queuePattern()` and `queueOf(String key)`, which extracts the queue name from a key, to keys.dart; have the client use them; write a pure keys test without Redis.
items.closure_criteria: client.dart builds every key through the new Keys helpers and spells no raw fragment such as :queue: or :inflight:. A pure keys test that runs without Redis covers the helpers and passes.

items.observation: `_dial` and `_send`, which reconnects once and wraps with `wrapRedisError`, are nearly line-for-line identical in the two classes; worker.dart:281 says 'Same rationale as [QueueClient._send]'. A fix can land on only one side.
items.proposed_fix: A small class that holds host/port/Command in a non-exported lib/src/connection.dart (send, reconnect, close); QueueClient and Worker delegate to it. test/connection_drop_test.dart already runs both paths.
items.closure_criteria: QueueClient and Worker delegate dialing and sending to one non-exported connection.dart class. test/connection_drop_test.dart still passes over both paths.

items.observation: `purgeDeadLetters` sends LLEN first and DEL second. A record the worker LPUSHes in between is deleted but not counted; the returned count under-reports the deletions. This violates RTQ-2.
items.proposed_fix: A single EVAL script (`local n = redis.call('LLEN', KEYS[1]) redis.call('DEL', KEYS[1]) return n`) as `static const _purgeScript`; add a count test to dead_letter_admin_test.
items.closure_criteria: purgeDeadLetters deletes and counts the list in one atomic _purgeScript EVAL. The new count test in dead_letter_admin_test passes.

items.observation: Inside `_process`, when `Envelope.decode` throws on a corrupt envelope, the loop's catch-all branch mistakes it for a lost connection: it sleeps for backoffBase, reconnects, and recovery skips the corrupt record with `continue`. The record stays in the in-flight list forever and inflates `stats().inFlight`. Found by reading the code; not reproduced by a run.
items.proposed_fix: Catch decode separately in `_process` with `on FormatException`/`on TypeError`, move the raw record to dead-letter through `_deadScript` with the error text; narrow the loop catch to `on TaskQueueException`; add an integration test that LPUSHes a corrupt record.
items.closure_criteria: A corrupt record LPUSHed to the in-flight list moves to dead-letter through _deadScript with the decode error text and no longer inflates stats().inFlight. The new integration test that LPUSHes a corrupt record passes.

items.observation: Seven bare `catch` blocks. Some are deliberate catch-alls (observer isolation at 600, handler error at 508) but none uses `on Object`; 462 should handle only decode errors.
items.proposed_fix: `on Object catch` plus the existing rationale comment; narrow 462 to `on FormatException` and 365 via RTQ-B4.
items.closure_criteria: No bare catch remains at the listed lines and each uses a typed on clause or on Object with a rationale comment. The package tests still pass.

items.observation: The envelope JSON map is written twice, in `encode` and in `encodeDead`; when a field is added, a dead-letter record can still be written in the old shape.
items.proposed_fix: A private `Map<String, Object?> _toJson()`; both use it. wire_format_test already pins the output.
items.closure_criteria: encode and encodeDead build their JSON map through one private _toJson. wire_format_test still passes.

items.observation: `DeadLetter.decode(String raw)` is public and exposed through `show DeadLetter`: wire format parsing has entered the user API. Only wire_format_test, which imports lib and src, uses it.
items.proposed_fix: Now: a non-API note in the dartdoc + CHANGELOG. Next major: move it to a function inside src. `package:meta` @internal would add a dependency and is rejected because of RTQ-8.
items.closure_criteria: The dartdoc and the CHANGELOG mark DeadLetter.decode as not part of the API. The next major version moves it to a function inside src that the show list does not export.

items.observation: `backoffJitter` is 0..1 in the dartdoc but is not validated; a weight of ≤0 silently drops out of queue sweeping; `backoffBase > backoffCap` is accepted. workerId is validated (231-233).
items.proposed_fix: `ArgumentError.value` checks at the start of `Worker.connect` + tests.
items.closure_criteria: Worker.connect throws ArgumentError.value for backoffJitter outside 0..1, for weights of zero or less and for backoffBase above backoffCap. The new argument tests pass.

items.observation: The `dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed .` step that the three sibling packages have is missing; two past 'Reformat' commits show that format drift has happened.
items.proposed_fix: Add a format step before analyze.
items.closure_criteria: ci.yml runs dart format --output=none --set-exit-if-changed before the analyze step. The format step passes on a clean checkout.

items.observation: Only lints/recommended; resilience and flutter_prerender enable strict-casts/inference/raw-types, public_member_api_docs and unawaited_futures. Undocumented public members (`close`, the `Task` constructor, `toJson`, `fromJson`) and an unresolved dartdoc reference `[enqueue]` (task.dart:143; the correct form is `[QueueClient.enqueue]`). The `Future<dynamic>` return of `_send` can produce findings in strict modes.
items.proposed_fix: Enable the resilience set and close the findings in the same change.
items.closure_criteria: analysis_options.yaml enables the strict lint set and dart analyze reports no findings. Every public member named in the item has dartdoc and the task.dart reference resolves to [QueueClient.enqueue].
